title: Kernel Switcher Heuristics + KV-shard / Quant-aware Routing Probe
content:
Purpose
Draft notes for a runtime-level "kernel switcher" that chooses between TensorRT, Triton, and our custom ops at request time. Focus: heuristics that are cheap to compute, interact sensibly with KV-cache sharding and quantization profiles, and minimize tail-latency regressions while preserving cost targets.

Background / motivation
- We have three primary execution backends: TensorRT (TRT) optimized kernels, Triton-backed model instances, and a lightweight custom-kernel path (cuda-ops + fused attention) used for some sequences and models.
- Current deployment has static routing by model-family + endpoint config. That leads to suboptimal unit economics: some low-token, short-seq workloads could be run on lower-cost custom-kernel configs, while long-seq generation benefits from TRT.
- KV cache distribution complicates this: moving a request to a different backend can cause either cache-miss warmup or extra memory transfers. We need a switcher that is aware of KV-shard locality and quantization compatibility.

High-level goals
- Decide per-request backend with <100us overhead (heuristic only, no full model introspection).
- Avoid decisions that cause full KV cache re-materialization except when expected net win > configured threshold.
- Respect quantization compatibility: do not route requests requiring int8 kernels to backends lacking that profile unless fallback permitted.
- Provide tunable policies per-customer and per-model: latency-first, cost-first, balanced.

Heuristics (proposal)
1) Fast decision inputs (all O(1) reads):
   - seq_len (prompt + expected gen)
   - requested max_tokens / streaming flag
   - client tier (free/dev/paid)
   - model variant tag (fp16/int8/ggml-style)
   - kv_cache_location: {local-shard-id, remote} and kv_hit_rate estimate (last N requests)
   - recent latency p90 for model on each backend (cached)

2) Decision rules (applied in order):
   a) Forced pins: if customer or route has explicit "force_backend" -> obey.
   b) Quantization mismatch block: if request requires a quant profile not available on backend -> exclude backend unless 'allow-approx'.
   c) KV locality penalty: if backend != kv_cache_location.shard then add penalty cost P_kv_move (ms) to predicted latency.
   d) Compute baseline latency estimate L_backend(seq_len, batch) from model profile table and add P_kv_move if applicable.
   e) Backend score = latency_score * latency_weight + cost_estimate * cost_weight (+ reliability_penalty). Choose min score.

3) Tunable knobs: latency_weight, cost_weight, P_kv_move, kv_rewarm_cost_estimate (tokens * per-token-cost-ms).

KV-shard specifics
- KV cache is sharded across N GPUs in a pool. Each shard holds prefix states for sessions pinned to that shard.
- Two modes: sticky-shard (preferred) and opportunistic-shard (allows moving request to less loaded shard with cache eviction/transfer).
- Heuristic: allow opportunistic migration only if predicted CPU+PCIe transfer + rewarm latency < (expected latency saving on backend) - epsilon. Use conservative epsilon (50ms) initially.
- When migrating: launch async prefetch of required KV pages (prefetch stream + priority) and mark request as 'warmup pending' and fall back to original shard for a small timeout if prefetch extends.

Quantization-aware routing
- Each backend advertises supported quant profiles (fp16, int8-ptq, int8-q4_0).
- If model served with multiple quant profiles, prefer backend that keeps requested quant profile to avoid inference-quality regressions.
- If request has 'quality: allow_lower' flag, allow fallback to lower-precision backend and expose a quality delta in response headers.

Fallback & safety
- If chosen backend queue depth > Q_high or observed backend p99 latency > SLA, fallback to next-best backend or a 'safe' CPU path.
- Maintain a small pool of standby Triton instances pre-warmed with top-K hot sessions to reduce cold-start KV pain.

Micro-benchmark plan (minimal experiments to evaluate heuristics)
1) Bench matrix: sequential runs for models: redwood-base-6b, redwood-13b, llama2-70b. Vary seq_len: 32/128/512/2048. Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8. Backends: TRT(fp16), Triton(fp16), Custom(fused-fp16). Metric: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-token estimate (based on GPU seconds). Also measure KV cache hit-rate and rewarm time when moving shards.
2) Small-scale migration probe: pick redwood-base-6b with sticky vs opportunistic shard policies. Force synthetic mix with 80% short seq, 20% long seq and measure overall tail latency and token cost.
3) Quant routing probe: run identical prompts with int8 vs fp16 profiles across backends, measure quality delta (perplexity / ngram-match) and latency delta.

Initial baseline numbers (from quick bench on dev-cluster, raw):
- redwood-base-6b seq128 batch1: TRT p50=42ms p90=78ms costUnit=0.7; Triton p50=60ms p90=110ms costUnit=0.9; Custom p50=48ms p90=90ms costUnit=0.5
- KV rewarm penalty observed (moving between GPUs): median 120ms, max 260ms for seq>1024
Notes: numbers are noisy, need repeat runs and cross-validate with infra traces.

Open questions / risks
- KV warmup variance: warmup cost strongly depends on how much prefix must be replayed vs. cached chunk transfer. Hard to model with a simple penalty term. Could introduce per-session NKV-size estimate to improve accuracy.
- Cold-start policy complexity: pre-warming too many standby sessions wastes memory. How do we pick top-K? heuristics based on recent RPS and session recency.
- Measurement bias: if our profiling table is built from experiments on a subset of hw configs, scheduler may mis-predict on different GPUs. Need per-cluster profiles and graceful fallback.
- Consistency with rollout: switching backend mid-rollout could hide regressions. Policy should prefer pinned backend during canary windows.

Implementation sketch
- New component: kernel-switcher service (stateless decision API) + local runtime cache of profile table and kv-shard map. Deployed as sidecar in Dedicated and Hosted nodes.
- Decision API inputs: route, seq_len, max_tokens, client_tier, kv_shard_hint, quant_profile, model_version
- Output: backend_name, estimated_latency_ms, estimated_cost, migrate_kv: true/false, migration_hint (shard id), reason_code
- Logging: record decision inputs, chosen backend, prediction score, actual observed latency for online calibration.

Telemetry & calibration
- Track per-decision calibration bucket: (model, seq_bin, backend) -> observed latency distribution. Use EWMA to adjust profile table numbers weekly.
- Add a "switch regret" counter: times where chosen backend incurred >X ms over best alternative; alert if >threshold.

Short-term action items (next 6 weeks)
- [ ] Run micro-bench matrix on redwood-base-6b and llama2-13b across dev-cluster (owner: Aisha) - target: 1 week to initial data
- [ ] Implement kernel-switcher prototype as a lightweight Rust service reading profile table from S3, sidecarable (owner: Marco) - target: 2 weeks
- [ ] Add basic opportunistic KV migration path in prototype (no prefetch) to measure rewarm penalty (owner: Noah) - target: 3 weeks
- [ ] Experiment with int8 routing flags and measure quality deltas (owner: Sana) - target: 3 weeks

Longer-term ideas
- ML-based meta-scheduler: train a small model to predict best backend given richer signals (recent per-session history, GPU occupancy, exact kv-size). But keep cheap heuristic as primary fallback.
- Proactive KV co-location: try to schedule frequently-correlated sessions on same shards to increase hit rate. (Needs higher-level placement and customer privacy considerations.)

Unresolved notes / TODOs
- Define exact formula for P_kv_move; current conservative default = 150ms. Need to derive from measured median rewarm + PCIe transfer.
- Add triggered trace collection for migrated requests for later analysis (stack + nvprof?).
- Decide storage format for profile table (binary vs JSON). JSON ok for early prototype.

Slack threads / references
- #serving-runtime: thread "kv-shard-migration-observations" (Dec 2024)
- PR: runtime/pull/842 for profile table v1
- Jira: ENG-1291 (kernel-switcher RFC)

Appendix: quick decision pseudocode
- function choose_backend(request):
    if request.pin_backend: return pinned
    candidates = list(backends) - unsupported_quant
    for b in candidates: score[b] = predict_latency(b, seq_len) + P_kv_move_if_remote(b) * latency_weight + cost_est(b) * cost_weight
    sort by score; chosen = candidates[0]
    if load(chosen) > Q_high: chosen = next_candidate; record fallback_reason
    return chosen

End
